issues.description: Constructor signature mismatch for Animal and its subclasses: The problem statement UML and the commented example in the template Main.java instantiate animals with a single String argument for the name (e.g., Seal("Clarabelle"), lines shown in template Main). The solution's Animal class declares a constructor public Animal(String name, int age) and the solution subclasses (e.g., Seal) likewise require (String, int). This difference (single-arg vs two-arg constructors) will cause the provided template Main example to fail to compile and will confuse students implementing constructors to match the UML/example.
issues.suggestedFix: Make constructor signatures consistent across artifacts. Preferred student-friendly fix: add single-argument constructors (String name) in Animal and corresponding single-arg constructors in each subclass (or provide overloads) so the template Main example compiles. Alternatively, update the problem statement and template Main to document and use two-argument constructors (String name, int age) in all examples and the UML.

issues.description: Attribute mismatch on class Animal: The UML and problem text specify that Animal has a name attribute (name: String) and tasks/examples imply only a name is required. The solution's Animal adds an extra field private int age; that is not present in the UML/problem and contributes to the constructor signature change. This structural difference changes the expected class shape and will confuse students following the UML and template examples.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the Animal attributes across artifacts. Either remove the 'age' field from the solution's Animal class so it matches the UML/problem, or update the problem statement and template Main to document the additional 'age' attribute and show two-argument constructors. A compatible approach is to keep 'age' but add overloads/constructors that accept only the name to avoid breaking the template examples.
